Proposed GitHub Releases fixture

Source: .github/live-release-fixture.md

Host the workflow and its R script in a dedicated fixture repository. Run it manually with workflow_dispatch or on a schedule. Give maintainers write access and protect its default branch. Run the job only on that branch. Keep the fixture repository name and the full, reviewed SATVILab/projr commit SHA in the trusted workflow. Updating the version under test takes a reviewed change to the pin. Use the fixture’s own trusted scripts and pin actions to reviewed SHAs.

Give the fixture job permissions: { contents: write } and use its short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN for release and tag operations in that repository. Set checkout’s persist-credentials: false. Supply the token to the release test and cleanup steps. Install the pinned projr revision and its dependencies before running the test. GitHub Actions token permissions

  1. Assert that GITHUB_REPOSITORY equals the fixture repository. Generate a fresh UUID in each invocation, including re-runs or simultaneous processes in the same job. Use projr-test-<UUID> for a single release. For the isolation check, append -a and -b to that invocation’s base tag. Address releases and assets by exact tag or ID throughout.
  2. For each tag, confirm that the exact release and tag ref are absent. Create a lightweight tag pointing at the known fixture commit (GITHUB_SHA), then a prerelease using projr’s .gh_release_create_httr(). Record the exact ref and its SHA immediately after confirmed tag creation, and the returned release ID and tag immediately after confirmed release creation. Keep these records in a file named for the invocation UUID in the runner temp directory and pass that path to cleanup. Abort on a collision. Only a successful creation response establishes ownership.
  3. Write two binary files with the same basename and different bytes. Create A and upload its file with .gh_release_asset_upload_httr(overwrite = FALSE). Create B and upload its file under the same asset name. Use .remote_ls_final_github_httr() and .remote_file_get_all_github_httr() on each exact tag. Verify the asset name, size and SHA-256 digest against its corresponding original in separate download directories.
  4. Delete A’s recorded release and tag. Confirm A is absent, then re-list and re-download B into an empty directory and verify B’s original bytes. This checks whether removing one release can affect another with an identically named asset.
  5. Use if: always() for final cleanup after success or failure. Process only the recorded release IDs and tag refs for this invocation. Verify the release’s tag and the ref’s target SHA, delete the release by ID and the tag by exact ref, and verify absence. Handle an already deleted owned object as success. Report unexpected API errors or ambiguous creation outcomes with the exact tag for inspection. All mutations target individual objects. GitHub Releases API and Git references API

Ordinary package checks and testthat runs exercise release behavior offline with fixtures or mocks. The dedicated release job uses the fixture repository’s scoped token.
